texts: mixed: the parse had to guess here - it split the date list into three separate hunts, one per day, which is almost certainly your meaning, but nothing settles whether coordinated date adjuncts give one hunt carrying three contradictory dates or three hunts, so the reading is not stable from run to run. Write one finite clause per day: 'Sky-cats hunted at the Sunken Cove on day 667 of Year 2, they hunted there on day 668 of Year 2, and they hunted there on day 669 of Year 2.'

bad: the thing asked for - 'permission' - is dropped entirely, and the 'to burn ...' clause is sealed as if it were a reported that-clause, which is not allowed for an infinitive; the permission then reappears as a status tag buried inside that seal, so what you asked for is recorded nowhere a question can reach it. Put the request as a finite question clause, which is a licensed sealing form and keeps the permission explicit: 'On day 670 of Year 2, Bevin Coombe asked the Council whether he was permitted to burn wintergloss at the Stilllight Lantern for one night.'

mixed: the approving itself is clean, but 'the test' mints a brand-new object with no link to the burning Bevin proposed, so nothing records what was approved - and sentence 11 inherits the same empty referent. Either name the act here: 'The Council allowed Bevin Coombe to burn wintergloss at the Stilllight Lantern for one night.' - or introduce the word earlier (end sentence 2 with '... for one night as a test') so 'the test' has an antecedent to point back to.

mixed: everything in this sentence parses - the doer, the alongside phrase, the mire-essence as part of the Lantern, sundown as the time - but bare 'wintergloss' is recorded as the substance-kind rather than as the specific quantity burned, and that is what leaves sentence 6's 'The wintergloss' with nothing to point at. Make it indefinite so a specific quantity is minted: 'Bevin Coombe burned some wintergloss alongside the mire-essence of the Stilllight Lantern at sundown.'
good. the Lantern is the doer of a produce event with mist-light as what it made, and mist-light also gets its 'is a kind of light' link.

bad: 'The wintergloss' is a specific definite, but the parse fills the doer slot with the bare substance-kind symbol, which is reserved for non-specific objects - a class ends up sitting where an individual belongs, and the coreference back to sentence 4 is lost. Fixing sentence 4 to 'some wintergloss' gives this definite a witness to reuse and this sentence then parses as written; if sentence 4 stays as it is, tie the reference in here instead: 'The wintergloss that Bevin Coombe burned repelled nightmoths from the Stilllight Lantern.'
good. the count rides a three-member nightmoth group, and 'that night' correctly picks up day 670 of Year 2 from the earlier sentence plus the night-part term.

bad: 'about twelve' has no licensed carrier - an exact count needs a plain whole number and the vague-quantity form is only for words with no number in them - so the parse typed a spread into the count slot, which is ill-formed and breaks the arithmetic our counting questions run. Drop the hedge or turn it into a bound: 'Twelve nightmoths gather at the Stilllight Lantern on a normal night.', or 'At least ten nightmoths gather at the Stilllight Lantern on a normal night.' if the approximation matters more than the figure. 'On a normal night' is fine as written - leave that part alone.
good. the denial covers both the group and each individual sky-cat, keeps the date and the night inside the denied bundle, and reuses the sky-cat group introduced in sentence 1.

mixed: the reporting parses with the right roles, but 'the result' is a fresh object with nothing tying it to the count in sentence 7, so 'what did he report?' comes back with an empty referent. Say the content instead: 'Bevin Coombe reported to the Council that he had counted three nightmoths at the Stilllight Lantern that night.'

mixed: the recording is clean and 'the test' does reuse sentence 3's object, so the two mentions are one thing - but that object is still never connected to the burning it names. Same fix as sentence 3: introduce 'a test' back in sentence 2, or name the act here: 'The Council recorded that Bevin Coombe had burned the wintergloss at the Stilllight Lantern for one night.'
